blocks.passage:
Running a cross-border transaction is a choreography. Orders are placed, documents are prepared, shipments move, payments are scheduled, and customers are informed — all in the right order, by the right people, at the right time.

The most common cause of problems is not lack of knowledge; it is lack of handoffs. The sales team books a deal but forgets to tell operations about a special delivery clause. Operations ship the goods but forget to tell finance the terms have changed. By the time the invoice arrives, it is wrong — and the customer is annoyed.

Good teams fix this with short, regular handoffs and a single source of truth per deal. Boring? Yes. But dramatic less often, which is exactly the point.

items.why: "Running a cross-border transaction is a choreography."

items.why: "The most common cause of problems is not lack of knowledge; it is lack of handoffs."

options: To tell operations about a special delivery clause
items.why: "The sales team books a deal but forgets to tell operations about a special delivery clause."

items.q: How do good teams fix the handoff problem?
options: With short, regular handoffs and a single source of truth per deal
items.why: "Good teams fix this with short, regular handoffs and a single source of truth per deal."

options: fewer crises through boring, reliable process
items.why: Inferência: processo chato e confiável = menos crises, que é o objetivo.

audio.text:
Let me show you why last week's shipment was invoiced wrong, because it's a textbook handoff failure — nobody was ignorant, the information just didn't travel.

Here's what happened. Sales closed the deal and, as part of it, agreed a change: the customer would pay in dollars, not euros, and get an extra 2% discount for a bigger volume. Good deal. But that change lived only in the salesperson's head and one email.

Operations shipped the goods perfectly — they didn't need to know about the pricing. But finance raised the invoice from the original order in the system, which still said euros, no discount. So the invoice went out wrong, and the customer, quite rightly, was annoyed.

Nobody here did anything stupid. The deal was fine, the shipping was fine. What failed was the handoff between sales and finance — the new terms never reached the person raising the invoice.

The fix is simple and boring: when sales changes any term, they update the single deal record, and finance always invoices from that record, never from memory or an old order. One source of truth, and this stops happening.

items.q: How does Emily describe the invoicing error?
items.why: "it's a textbook handoff failure — nobody was ignorant, the information just didn't travel."

options: Payment in dollars, not euros, plus a 2% discount for bigger volume

options: Finance invoiced from the original order, which still said euros with no discount
items.why: "finance raised the invoice from the original order in the system, which still said euros, no discount."

items.q: What actually failed?
options: The handoff between sales and finance
items.why: "What failed was the handoff between sales and finance."

items.q: What is the fix Emily proposes?
options: Sales updates one deal record; finance always invoices from that record
items.why: "they update the single deal record, and finance always invoices from that record."

items.q: A **handoff** between teams is…
options: the passing of work or information from one to another
items.why: Handoff = passagem de bastão.

items.q: A **single source of truth** is…
options: one authoritative record everyone relies on
items.why: Source of truth = fonte única e confiável da informação.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Sales must **___** operations about the special clause."
items.why: To brief = informar/orientar.

items.q: "It's a **cross-border** transaction." Cross-border means…
items.why: Cross-border = transfronteiriço.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A clear **___** prevents work from being dropped between teams."
items.why: Workflow = fluxo de trabalho.

items.q: "The information **fell through the cracks**." To fall through the cracks means to…
items.why: Fall through the cracks = escapar, ser esquecido.

items.q: "Let's **loop in** finance before invoicing." To loop in means to…
items.why: Loop in = incluir na comunicação.

items.q: "Sales **dropped the ball** on telling finance." To drop the ball means to…
options: fail to do something you were responsible for
items.why: Drop the ball = vacilar, falhar numa responsabilidade.

items.q: "Finance invoiced **from memory**." To do something from memory means to…
options: rely on what you remember, not a record
items.why: From memory = de cabeça, sem conferir o registro.

items.q: "Let's **keep everyone on the same page**." To be on the same page means to…
items.why: On the same page = alinhados, mesmo entendimento.
